rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that the process ends once a completion step has been carried out successfully, and that a later occurrence (such as feedback or a return) may follow after the end: Model the completion step as its own task on the main flow, placed directly before a single end event. Name the end event for the process end, not for the outcome. Model the later occurrence as a separate task or branch that is joined to the main flow through a gateway, and do not fold it into the label of the end event.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description's closing sentence reports that a party begins its own further activity after an earlier step is completed, so the final described step is the start of work and not a terminal state

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the process ends once a handover or allocation step has been completed, and then names an actor beginning a further activity as part of that ending: Model the named follow-on activity as its own task on the main flow, placed directly before the end event, so the end event follows that task. Do not drop the follow-on activity or end the flow right after the preceding step.
